Why go: Samui's quiet south-west on horseback

Taling Ngam, on Koh Samui's south-west coast, is far from the resort strips: coconut groves, a long, calm beach and views to the Five Islands and Ang Thong. Riding there at sunset is one of the most memorable ways to see it, and you don't need to be an experienced rider.

What you'll do

After a welcome drink and a helmet fitting, a guide matches each rider to a horse based on the level you give us. The group follows the guide along coastal trails and onto the beach at a walk, with trotting for confident riders. Beginners and children ride with a staff member leading the horse. Choose 30 minutes for a first try or 60 minutes for the full route, ideally the 17:00 sunset ride.

Who it suits

  • Couples looking for a sunset activity away from the crowds.
  • Families with children from 5, as each child can have a horse-leader.
  • Guests staying in Taling Ngam, Lipa Noi or the south, where the drive is short.

Who should choose something else

  • Riders over 90 kg, which is the stable's limit for the horses' welfare.
  • Couples staying in Chaweng on a budget: the compulsory van makes it expensive for two. A sunset cruise may be better value.

Good to know

  • Welfare: a weight limit, no midday rides and walking pace on the beach are good signs. Tell us if anything about the horses' condition worries you.
  • Weather: in heavy rain or rough seas the stable may move your ride to another time.
  • Getting there: Taling Ngam is about 45–60 minutes from Chaweng; the compulsory van covers this and waits for 1 hour.
